Palestinian officials and witnesses say Israeli settlers
set fire to cars and homes overnight
in the Israeli-occupied West Bank.
A top Israeli politician is calling it Jewish terrorism.
NPR's Lauren Fair reports.

to the, quote, "brink of unchecked anarchy."
Eisenkot is leading coalition talks to oust
Israel's far-right Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu,
who has extremist settlers in his cabinet.

The UN accuses Netanyahu's government

Lauren Frier, NPR News, Tel Aviv.

United Nations climate talks in Turkey have broken down
without a broad agreement.
The European Union and several countries rejected a draft
that made no mention of coal, oil, or natural gas.
Russia and Saudi Arabia had pushed to keep fossil fuels
out of the agreement.
The deadlock held, even as negotiations stretch
nearly two days past their scheduled end.
After traveling for more than eight years,

around the planet Mercury.
The probe should provide scientists with a wealth

in the solar system.
Joe Palka reports.
Mercury is an intriguing planet.
It has an incredible number of scientific mysteries.
Anne Pomier at the Carnegie Institution

She says scientists have found evidence
that there is ice at the poles of the planet,
odd for a planet so close to the sun.
It also has a larger metal core than expected.
The fact that this planet is shrinking

Bepi-Colombo is scheduled to start answering
